title: The upper to deep oxygen-nitrate contrast rose on A20 and A22 in 2012-2021 under a fixed 170:16 ratio and uniform cruise error bounds
abstract: We tested whether oxygen loss on sigma0 26.5 can be explained by oxygen use at fixed nutrient ratios and fixed initial water properties. We used joint flag-2 oxygen, nitrate and phosphate bottles from GLODAPv2.2023 on A20 and A22 in 26-36 N. The combination NO = oxygen + (170/16) nitrate cancels fixed-ratio oxygen consumption without a water age model. In 2012-2021, upper NO rose by 7.70 and 7.52 micromol/kg on the same-cast subset. The upper minus 4,000 m contrast rose by 10.85 (conditional 95% interval 9.31 to 12.11) on A20 and 8.78 (7.55 to 10.15) on A22. Arbitrary additive cruise offsets cancel in this vertical contrast. Under adverse uniform shifts of up to 1% oxygen and 2% nitrate on each cruise, the contrasts were 3.47 (2.14 to 4.52) and 1.81 (0.64 to 3.15). The 97.5th percentile thresholds for the oxygen-to-nitrate coefficient were 9.51 and 10.24; lower coefficients do not support the same error-controlled result. Phosphate tests were less robust. BATS annual context data did not reproduce the same nutrient pattern. The fixed-property, fixed-ratio model fails for the sampled vertical change under the stated error bounds. Source changes, gas exchange history, nutrient ratios and errors remain possible causes. A real deep change can affect the contrast, so an upper source-property change is not identified with unrestricted additive error and deep change. Two occupations, ten bins per line, sparse profiles and untested depth-dependent errors limit the result. Code, aggregate results, independent audits and a clean reproduction report are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Changes in the oxygen-nutrient combinations on the upper surface, at 4,000 m, and in the vertical contrast. Bars give conditional 95% joint latitude-block intervals. The same casts enter both levels.

The oxygen-nitrate contrast depends on the assumed ratio and uniform cruise error bounds. The dotted lines give the 97.5th percentiles of the minimum coefficient needed to keep the adverse vertical contrast positive. Shaded limits connect tested coefficients.
